context: Agents are defined as contracts (AGENTS/*/agent.json) and materialized into OpenCode assets (ADR-0017). The Master System versions itself (VERSION 0.4.0, DOCS/versioning.md). The lifecycle of agent contracts (new, change, deprecate) is not yet defined, so changes can happen silently and drift from generated assets.
problem: How are agent contracts introduced, changed and deprecated across Master System releases while keeping generated OpenCode assets and project compatibility in sync?

options_considered.option: Version agents with the OS; contract change requires ADR + bump + regeneration
pros: Generated assets always match a declared version

cons: Silent drift and breakage of downstream projects

decision: Agent lifecycle is bound to Master System releases. Adding/renaming/deprecating an agent contract is a material change requiring an ADR, a VERSION bump (per DOCS/VERSIONING_STRATEGY.md), updated AGENTS/README.md, regeneration of OpenCode assets, and updated tests. Interactions that would weaken a gate are forbidden; new agent permissions are the intersection with task authorized_actions and never grant DESTRUCTIVE. Compatibility: PROJECT.json.master_system_version declares the floor version the project expects.
reason: It makes agent evolution auditable, prevents silent drift, ties generated assets to versions, and preserves the gate and security invariants (restrictions 5, 6, 7).
consequences: Regeneration and drift checks are part of release and CI. Deprecation keeps the asset but marks it; removal requires a major (or 0.x-minor) bump per the versioning strategy.
